## 6. Lean Code Style

A single account cannot approve its own pull request, so GitHub's review-state
field carries no authority here (`issues-prs.md` §2): the verdict is a trailer
in the agent's last message (`codex exec -o <file>`), and the contract demands
three things in order:

1. a `## Findings` section, one line per finding, in exactly this shape:

       - [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/Path/File.lean:123` — one-line summary

   with severity in {`blocker`, `changes`, `advisory`} and `-` in place of
   `path:line` when a finding is not tied to a line; or the single line
   `- none`;
2. a `## Review` section with the prose;
3. as the final line, alone:

       VERDICT: APPROVED | COMMENTED | CHANGES_REQUESTED

A missing or malformed trailer is **not** an approval: `review.sh` exits 4,
posts a `failure` `local-review/summary`, and keeps the raw output under
`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr<N>/<sha>/`.  Nothing in the findings section
is discarded either — a line that does not parse is kept verbatim as a
`changes`-severity finding labelled `unparsed finding:`, and a non-approving
verdict with an empty ledger gets one synthesised finding so the merge gate
still blocks.  Both rules follow the same principle as rung 5: the failure mode
worth engineering against is a review that reads green without having happened.

## 7. Which reviews run

* **Code review** always.  `pr-review.yml` ran it as a matrix over
  `CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS` (anthropic, deepseek).  Locally the matrix
  collapses to one codex session; a second backend can be added by running
  `review.sh` again with `MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL` set, which writes a separate
  per-SHA file only if you also change the file name, so treat multi-provider
  review as unimplemented rather than as a one-liner.
* **Prose review** only when the diff touches `blueprint/`.  On GitHub it ran
  unconditionally on a cheaper tier; gating it on the diff is a local
  cost decision, not a weakening — the prose prompt reviews blueprint ↔ Lean
  equivalence and blueprint prose, and a diff that touches no blueprint file
  has nothing for it to review.  Set `MIPSTARRE_PROSE_MODEL` for the
  cheaper-tier split.

The failure semantics of the two are deliberately different, and the difference
is inherited: `pr-review.yml:112-131` *fails* the code review when its token is
missing, while `pr-review.yml:202-224` *skips* the prose review in the same
situation.  Locally, a code reviewer that dies without output blocks the PR; a
prose reviewer that dies leaves a warning and the code verdict stands.

The published verdict takes the **worst** of the two lanes, written verbatim on
the `VERDICT:` line of one exact-head `COMMENT` review (marker
`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->`): `APPROVED`, `COMMENTED` or
`CHANGES_REQUESTED`.  Adverse verdicts post as `COMMENT` too; adverseness lives
in the paired `local-review/summary` status, `success` only for `APPROVED` or a
`COMMENTED` verdict with an empty ledger and `failure` otherwise.  A head with
no review at all simply has no such status, which the merge gate reads as
"not reviewed" rather than as a pass.

## 8. Concurrency

| Lock | Key | Cancellation |
|---|---|---|
| review | PR id | none — a queued run waits, then re-checks the head |
| fix (`autofix.md`) | branch | supersession sentinel |

The split of keys is inherited (`pr-review.yml:18-20` groups by PR number with
`cancel-in-progress: false`; `auto-fix.yml:259-261` groups by head branch with
`cancel-in-progress: true`) and it matters: cancelling a review wastes the
tokens already spent and produces nothing, whereas cancelling a superseded fix
saves a write to a branch that has already moved.

Locks are directories under `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/` holding the
holder's pid — `flock(1)` does not exist on macOS.  A lock whose holder is gone
is reclaimed.  After acquiring the review lock, `review.sh` re-reads the local
tip and the remote PR head: a fix commit that landed while this run queued
invalidates the review, and the run exits without a verdict rather than
describing a commit that is no longer head.  The same check runs again after
the agent returns; a head that moved during the review makes the result stale
and forbids publication, leaving the raw output in the runtime cache.

`review.sh` also refuses to start while a fix lock is held for the branch.
The two tools share one worktree here, where GitHub gave each job a fresh
checkout; without this cross-check the reviewer would read a tree being
rewritten under it.

## 9. The findings ledger

`docs/pr_review_management.md` records the audit failure this replaces:
review feedback lived on three separate GitHub surfaces — inline
`pulls/N/comments`, issue-level `issues/N/comments`, and review summaries
`pulls/N/reviews` — and PRs were merged with comments nobody had read.  The
GraphQL `reviewThreads` `isResolved` / `isOutdated` pair was the only reliable
status signal; the REST `line` field lied.

Locally there is **one** surface.  Every finding lives on one line of the
`## Findings` section of the exact-head `COMMENT` review body, between
`<!-- findings:begin -->` and `<!-- findings:end -->`:

    - [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/Basic.lean:120` — adds a non-paper hypothesis

| Box | Meaning | Blocks merge |
|---|---|---|
| `[ ]` | unresolved | **yes** |
| `[x]` | resolved — a human or an agent addressed it and says so | no |
| `[-]` | outdated — the cited lines were rewritten since the reviewed SHA | no |

`[ ]` → `[x]` is a human judgement, or a claim by the fixer that a human is
expected to check; it is never automatic.  There is no automatic `[ ]` → `[-]`
pass: exactly one review is published per head SHA and the merge gate reads only
that one, so a finding written against an older SHA can no longer block and has
nothing to be outdated *out of*.  `[-]` stays available as a hand-written
disposition; a reviewer re-derives its findings from the new diff on every head.

**Merge gate.**  A PR whose current-head review carries any `[ ]` finding is
not mergeable.  The contract for `pr_merge.py` and for humans is exactly the
unchecked-finding regex of `issues-prs.md` §2, `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`, applied to
the marker-bound review body for the head SHA; no match means the ledger is
clean, and the paired `local-review/summary` status must agree.  Anything else
must be resolved, outdated, or adjudicated by the operator under §12 (Round cap
and operator adjudication) — the operator is the adjudicating party; the owner
is consulted only for the escalations named in the standing briefing.  Owner
decision 2026-09-02 (EVOLUTION.md): this supersedes the GitHub-era "never merge
without consulting the user" rule of `docs/pr_review_management.md` for this
repository; the substantive review criteria are unchanged.

Findings do **not** survive across SHAs.  Gate 4 matches the marker
`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->` on that exact commit id, so a ledger
written at SHA *A* is invisible at SHA *B* — and a head carrying no review at
all is "not reviewed", never clean.  A finding that still applies is one the
next review re-derives from the new diff.

A second review of the **same** SHA replaces that SHA's ledger, including any
`[x]` a human had set.  `review.sh` copies the previous file into the run
directory as `<name>.superseded` and warns when it did so, but it does not
merge the two ledgers: a re-review is a new opinion about the same commit, and
silently carrying resolutions across it would let a resolved-then-reintroduced
finding disappear.  Resolve findings on the SHA you intend to keep.

## 10. `agent.sh` versus `autofix.sh`

`docs/pr_review_management.md` keeps a behavioural matrix for the `@claude` and
`@codex` responders — mentions fire only from comments and never from bodies;
`@codex` on an issue always forks a fresh PR from `main`, causing PR
proliferation; `@claude` on a PR pushes to the branch but failed outright on
branch names containing `]`, root-caused to `claude-code-action`'s branch-name
validation and fixed by adopting bracket-free naming
(`docs/pr_review_management.md:163`, `CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124`).

The local translation is:

| Parent | Local | Who starts it |
|---|---|---|
| `@claude` on a PR comment | `local/bin/agent.sh <pr-id> "instruction"` | a human, always |
| `@codex` on an issue | `local/bin/agent.sh <issue-id> "instruction"` | a human, always |
| auto-fix workflows | `local/bin/autofix.sh <pr-id> --mode ...` | CI/review chain or a human |

`agent.sh` is **never invoked by automation.**  `claude.yml:24-30` gated the
responder on `sender.type != 'Bot'` because a bot echoing `@claude` into a
comment would start a write-enabled, secret-bearing session; the local form is
that `review.sh` and `autofix.sh` export `MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION=1` (and
`MIPSTARRE_AUTOFIX_ACTIVE=1`) around every agent they run, and `agent.sh`
refuses to start when either is set.  `agent.sh` also refuses while a fix lock
is held for its branch: two writers on one branch is the parallel-push
collision that `auto-fix.yml:253-256` serialised away.

The author_association gate has no local analogue and is dropped — the human
running the command *is* the authorisation.  The `]`-in-branch-name lesson
survives as a lint in all three scripts.

`agent.sh` may commit; it must not use the `[codex-auto-fix]` /
`[codex-review-fix]` prefixes, because a human-directed commit must be
reviewable and those prefixes make the reviewer skip.  The script warns if the
session used one anyway.

The auto-create-PR step of `claude.yml` becomes a printed instruction rather
than an action: when a session on an issue branch produces commits, `agent.sh`
tells the operator to open the PR with `local/bin/pr_open.py`, which pushes the
branch and owns the branch-name lint (`local/protocols/issues-prs.md`).

## 11. Operating it

    local/bin/review.sh 7                # review PR 0007 at its current head
    local/bin/review.sh 7 --dry-run      # build diff and prompts, dispatch nothing
    LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED=false local/bin/review.sh 7    # confirm the kill switch

Exit codes: `0` reviewed or intentionally skipped · `1` usage/environment ·
`3` gate blocked (CI not green for this head) · `4` no parseable verdict.
Code 3 publishes nothing at all — the missing green `local-review/summary` is
the block.  Only code 4 publishes a `failure` `local-review/summary`, and
neither publishes a review.

Artefacts:

| Path | Committed | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| the exact-head `COMMENT` review on the PR | on GitHub | combined verdict, ledger, prose |
| `local-review/summary` on the head SHA | on GitHub | the gate-readable verdict |
| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr<N>/<sha>/` | no | diff, prompts, raw agent output |
| `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/review-<pr>.lock` | no | the review lock |

Every codex invocation goes through `local/bin/dispatch.sh` when it exists, so
the session is named, captured to `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl` and
summarised into `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl`
(`local/protocols/sessions.md`).  Without the dispatcher, `review.sh` falls
back to a direct `codex exec` and says loudly that the session will not appear
in the registry — an untracked session is lost research data, so the fallback
is a degradation, not an alternative.  `dispatch.sh` enforces
`LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` for reviewer-role sessions independently; the two checks
agreeing is intentional redundancy.

Missing pieces degrade with a message, never silently: missing CI statuses
block, no `worktree-setup.sh` warns about a cold build cache, no codex CLI is a
hard error.  A GitHub failure is fatal — a verdict that cannot be published is
not a verdict.

## 12. Deliberately not ported

Untouched-code or new-mechanism findings are "out of scope -> issue #N".

* **Provider matrix** (`CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS` → per-provider jobs).
  One reviewer session; the cascade
  `CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS > CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER > anthropic` becomes
  `MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL > MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL > the dispatcher's default`.
* **Fork check** (`head_repository.full_name != repo` → skip).  Every PR here
  comes from a branch of this single repository.
* **Thread resolution via `mcp__github__resolve_review_thread`.**  Replaced by
  the ledger checkbox; the reviewer is told not to attempt it.
* **`allowed-tools` presets and `allowed-tools.json`.**  codex sandbox modes
  (`read-only` for review, `workspace-write` for fixes) carry the same intent
  with a coarser grain: read-only genuinely prevents writes, which the
  allow-list only approximated.
* **`id-token`/OAuth plumbing, `LionSR/agent-ci-actions`, plugin marketplaces.**
  Local codex configuration replaces them (`.codex/`, `local/protocols/sessions.md`).


## 12. Round cap and operator adjudication (2026-08-30)

A PR receives at most **four** full review rounds. From the fifth round on,
the operator may close the loop by adjudication instead of iteration:

1. every remaining finding is either fixed, or converted to a tracked issue;
   the operator posts an **ADJUDICATION comment** on the PR — a body starting
   with `ADJUDICATION`, carrying `head=<final_head>`, and listing the last
   round's findings with every box ticked and a one-line disposition each
   (`fixed in <commit>` / `deferred to issue #NNNN: <reason>` /
   `moot: <reason>`);
2. the comment is the record; nothing local is written;
3. the merge commit names the adjudication and the issues created;
4. `pr_merge.py --adjudicated` accepts it in place of a clean verdict, and
   only for the current head — a stale `head=` is a refusal.

Nothing is dropped silently: an adjudicated finding lives on as an issue.
This mirrors the parent's combined bot-fix iteration cap with a single
terminal review (pr-review.yml:69-72). See EVOLUTION.md for the trigger.

## 13. Evidence follows the diff: carry-forward across a fresh-base (2026-09-04)

The merge gate's fresh-base rule (issues-prs.md, gate 2b) moves a PR's head
every time `main` advances, but a merge of `main` into the branch does not
change the PR's own patch.  `review.sh` therefore compares a whitespace-
sensitive hash of the patch (the diff without its `index`/hunk-header lines,
so hunk positions may move but no byte of content may) with that of every
earlier reviewed head of the same PR whose review is bound to that head and
published by the lane's account; on a match it republishes that head's verdict
and ledger as the exact-head review of the new head, marked "Carried forward
from <sha>" (marker `<!-- mipstarre-review-carried from=<sha> -->`; a carried
review is not a review round and is never itself a carry source), and posts the matching
`local-review/summary` — without dispatching the reviewer.  Adverse verdicts
are carried too, so an adjudication at the new head remains possible.  Any
change to the patch (a repair, a conflict resolution) yields a different
patch-id and a real review.  `--force-review` bypasses the fast path.

   114	def ensure_mergeable_worktree(repo_root: Path, branch: str, base: str, head_sha: str) -> None:
   115	    """Gate 2 — clean primary worktree on the base, local branch at the head.
   116	
   117	    GitHub performs the merge, so none of this is needed for the merge itself; all of it
   118	    is needed for the tail, which fast-forwards ``base`` in this very worktree and
   119	    deletes the branch.  Refusing here keeps the failure before the irreversible step.
   120	    """
   121	    dirty = git(repo_root, "status", "--porcelain")
   122	    if dirty:
   123	        raise GateFailure("gate 2 (worktree): the primary tree is not clean, required clean "
   124	                          "so the post-merge fast-forward cannot lose work:\n" + dirty)
   125	    current = git(repo_root, "rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD")
   126	    if current != base:
   127	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 2 (worktree): HEAD is on {current!r}, required {base!r} "
   128	                          f"(the PR base). Run: git switch {base}")
   129	    tip = git(repo_root, "rev-parse", "--verify", f"{branch}^{{commit}}", check=False)
   130	    if not tip:
   131	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 2 (local branch): {branch!r} does not resolve here, required "
   132	                          f"it at {head_sha[:12]}: git fetch github {branch}:{branch}")
   133	    if tip != head_sha:
   134	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 2 (local branch): {branch} tip is {tip[:12]}, required "
   135	                          f"{head_sha[:12]} (the PR head). Push or fetch — the evidence binds "
   136	                          "to the SHA, not to the branch name.")
   137	    passed(f"gate 2 worktree clean on {base}, local tip == head")

   152	                          f"{len(CI_CONTEXTS)} contexts; observed:\n  " + "\n  ".join(problems)
   153	                          + "\nRun local/bin/ci.sh on this head. A missing context is a block, "
   154	                          "never a pass: GitHub's combined state is 'success' for a commit "
   155	                          "with no statuses at all.")

   159	def check_review(number: int, head_sha: str, reviews: list[dict], statuses: dict,
   160	                 *, adjudicated: bool) -> None:
   161	    """Gate 4 — one verdict review on this commit id, clean or adjudicated."""
   162	    marker = f"<!-- mipstarre-review pr={number} head={head_sha} -->"
   163	    matching = [r for r in reviews
   164	                if r.get("commit_id") == head_sha and marker in (r.get("body") or "")]
   165	    if not matching:
   166	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 4 (review): no review carrying {marker} on commit "
   167	                          f"{head_sha[:12]}, required exactly one. A verdict on an earlier SHA "
   168	                          "does not carry over (DESIGN.md:66-69): re-run review.sh.")
   169	    # One verdict review per head is the contract; if a retry ever leaves two, the newest
   170	    # is operative (the API returns reviews in creation order).
   171	    body = matching[-1].get("body") or ""
   172	    found = VERDICT_RE.search(body)
   173	    verdict = found.group(1) if found else ""
   174	    unchecked = len(UNCHECKED_FINDING_RE.findall(body))
   175	    summary_state = (statuses.get(REVIEW_CONTEXT) or {}).get("state")
   176	    # Green needs BOTH a clean verdict and a clean ledger: an APPROVED trailer
   177	    # over unresolved findings is inconsistent reviewer output (round 2, F4).
   178	    clean = verdict in ("APPROVED", "COMMENTED") and unchecked == 0
   179	    if clean and summary_state == "success":
   180	        passed(f"gate 4 verdict {verdict} on {head_sha[:12]}, {REVIEW_CONTEXT} success")
   181	        return
   182	    observed = (f"VERDICT {verdict or 'absent'} with {unchecked} unchecked finding(s), "
   183	                f"{REVIEW_CONTEXT} {summary_state or 'MISSING'}")
   184	    if not adjudicated:
   185	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 4 (review): required VERDICT APPROVED, or COMMENTED with zero "
   186	                          f"unchecked findings, and {REVIEW_CONTEXT} success; observed "
   187	                          f"{observed}. Address the findings (or tick them off with a reason and "
   188	                          "a tracked issue) and re-run review.sh, or merge --adjudicated.")
   189	    # review.md section 12: past the round cap the operator may adjudicate what is left.
   190	    # Binding the comment to the SHA stops an adjudication of round four covering five.
   191	    where = None
   192	    for row in gh_common.api(f"issues/{number}/comments", paginate=True):

   194	        if text.startswith("ADJUDICATION") and f"head={head_sha}" in text:

   196	            break
   197	    if where is None:
   198	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 4 (review): --adjudicated given but no ADJUDICATION comment "
   199	                          f"names head={head_sha} on PR #{number}; observed {observed}. Post one "
   200	                          f"first: a comment starting with ADJUDICATION, containing that head.")
   201	    sys.stderr.write(f"warning: merging PR #{number} on operator adjudication ({where}); the "
   202	                     f"review evidence is adverse — {observed}\n")
   203	    passed(f"gate 4 adjudicated at {head_sha[:12]} ({where})")

   206	def check_fix_gates(repo_root: Path, branch: str, base: str, head_sha: str) -> str:
   207	    """Gate 6 — refuse while the serialized fix loop is mid-flight.
   208	    Returns the merge base (gate 7 scans the same commit range); the fix-prefixed
   209	    commit count is reported, never enforced (EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-02)."""
   210	    # autofix.sh holds a mkdir-based lease keyed on the BRANCH (autofix.sh:580,
   211	    # locks/fix-<branch with / -> ->.lock, holder pid in <lock>/pid).  Probe the same lock
   212	    # the same way; a dead holder's lock does not block the merge.
   213	    lock = lock_dir() / ("fix-" + branch.replace("/", "-") + ".lock")
   214	    if lock.is_dir():
   215	        pid_text = ""
   216	        try:
   217	            pid_text = (lock / "pid").read_text(encoding="ascii").split()[0]
   218	        except (OSError, IndexError):
   219	            pass
   220	        if pid_text.isdigit() and _pid_alive(int(pid_text)):
   221	            raise GateFailure(f"gate 6 (fix loop): {lock} is held by live pid {pid_text}, required "
   222	                              "idle. autofix.sh is rewriting this branch and merging under it "
   223	                              "would race the fix commits.")
   224	    base_ref = None
   225	    for candidate in (f"github/{base}", f"refs/remotes/origin/{base}", base):
   226	        if git_ok(repo_root, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", f"{candidate}^{{commit}}"):
   227	            base_ref = candidate
   228	            break
   229	    if base_ref is None:
   230	        raise GateFailure(f"gate 7 (dependencies): no local ref resolves for base {base!r}, so "
   231	                          f"the merge-base commit range cannot be scanned. Run: git fetch "
   232	                          f"github {base}")
   233	    merge_base = git(repo_root, "merge-base", base_ref, head_sha)
   234	    # `git rev-list --format` prints a "commit <sha>" header before each formatted line.
   235	    lines = git(repo_root, "rev-list", "--format=%s", f"{merge_base}..{head_sha}").splitlines()
   236	    iterations = sum(1 for line in lines if not line.startswith("commit ")
   237	                     and line.startswith(FIX_COMMIT_PREFIXES))
   238	    passed(f"gate 6 fix loop idle; {iterations} fix-prefixed commit(s) since "
   239	           f"{merge_base[:12]} (autofix.sh bounds its own loop)")
   240	    return merge_base

1-#!/usr/bin/env bash
2-#
3-# autofix.sh — serialized, capped auto-fix loop for a local PR.
4-#
5-# Usage:
6-#   local/bin/autofix.sh <pr-id> --mode {ci|blueprint|review|auto} [--dry-run]
7-#
8-#   <pr-id>     GitHub PR number, e.g. "7" (GitHub is the source of truth for
9-#               PR metadata now; there is no local PR record).
10-#   --mode ci         fix Lean build errors, if local-ci/build failed on the head
11-#          blueprint  fix blueprint compilation, if that CI step failed
12:#          review     fix unresolved review findings (needs the auto-fix label)
13-#          auto       dispatch from the head's CI statuses and run every
14-#                     applicable fix strictly in the order ci -> blueprint -> review
15-#   --dry-run   Resolve the dispatch and build the prompts, then stop.
16-#
17-# Local replacement for .github/workflows/auto-fix.yml (setup + auto-fix-ci +
18-# auto-fix-blueprint + auto-fix-review).  Protocol: local/protocols/autofix.md.
19-#
20-# Exit codes:
21-#   0  fixes applied, or an intentional skip (kill switch, nothing to fix,
22-#      superseded by a newer run, iteration cap reached)
23-#   1  usage or environment error
24-#   2  a fix phase failed (agent error, or a rejected commit)
25-#
26-# Environment:
27-#   LOCAL_AUTO_FIX_ENABLED    disables every fix path on the literal string
28-#                             "false" only; unset means enabled.
29-#   MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP         combined fix-iteration cap (default 5)
30-#   MIPSTARRE_TRUSTED_REF     git ref the fixer personas are read from
31-#                             (default: main).  Never the branch being fixed.
32-#   MIPSTARRE_FIX_MODEL       codex model (default: the dispatcher's default)
33-#   MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT       runtime state root (default ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev)

   253	| `[-]` | outdated — the cited lines were rewritten since the reviewed SHA | no |
   254	
   255	`[ ]` → `[x]` is a human judgement, or a claim by the fixer that a human is
   256	expected to check; it is never automatic.  There is no automatic `[ ]` → `[-]`
   257	pass: exactly one review is published per head SHA and the merge gate reads only
   258	that one, so a finding written against an older SHA can no longer block and has
   259	nothing to be outdated *out of*.  `[-]` stays available as a hand-written
   260	disposition; a reviewer re-derives its findings from the new diff on every head.
   261	
   262	**Merge gate.**  A PR whose current-head review carries any `[ ]` finding is
   263	not mergeable.  The contract for `pr_merge.py` and for humans is exactly the
   264	unchecked-finding regex of `issues-prs.md` §2, `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`, applied to
   265	the marker-bound review body for the head SHA; no match means the ledger is
   266	clean, and the paired `local-review/summary` status must agree.  Anything else
   267	must be resolved, outdated, or adjudicated by the operator under §12 (Round cap
   268	and operator adjudication) — the operator is the adjudicating party; the owner
   269	is consulted only for the escalations named in the standing briefing.  Owner
   270	decision 2026-09-02 (EVOLUTION.md): this supersedes the GitHub-era "never merge
   271	without consulting the user" rule of `docs/pr_review_management.md` for this
   272	repository; the substantive review criteria are unchanged.
   273	
   274	Findings do **not** survive across SHAs.  Gate 4 matches the marker
   275	`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->` on that exact commit id, so a ledger
   276	written at SHA *A* is invisible at SHA *B* — and a head carrying no review at
   277	all is "not reviewed", never clean.  A finding that still applies is one the
   278	next review re-derives from the new diff.
   279	
   280	A second review of the **same** SHA replaces that SHA's ledger, including any
   281	`[x]` a human had set.  `review.sh` copies the previous file into the run
   282	directory as `<name>.superseded` and warns when it did so, but it does not
   283	merge the two ledgers: a re-review is a new opinion about the same commit, and
   284	silently carrying resolutions across it would let a resolved-then-reintroduced
   285	finding disappear.  Resolve findings on the SHA you intend to keep.

    50	`local-ci/<step>` per CI step (`build`, `blueprint-render`, `paper-gaps`,

    59

    62	line `VERDICT: APPROVED | COMMENTED | CHANGES_REQUESTED (code=…, prose=…)`.
    63	Unchecked findings are ledger lines matching `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`; clean means

getconf ARG_MAX -> 2097152      # irrelevant: it is the total, not per-arg
131071 bytes -> OK
131072 bytes -> FAIL [Errno 7] Argument list too long
200000 bytes -> FAIL
```

- pr5 (all four heads): 102,180–105,121 B → prompt ≈ 124 KB → within **7 KB (6%)** of the cliff. A slightly longer task or diff tips it over.

tail: "... [8437 further lines omitted by review.sh; full text on disk]"
```

ledger = ["- [ ] F%d (%s) `%s` — %s" % (n, sev, loc, summary) ...]
```
`LINE_BT`/`LINE_PL` capture the reviewer's checkbox as group(1) and never read it. The proposal's ~10 lines are all prompt text and do not touch 728, so a reviewer emitting `- [x] F13 (advisory)` still yields `- [ ] F13 (advisory)`, combine_review copies it verbatim, the `UNCHECKED` regex counts it, and `pr_merge.py:63/174` blocks. Net behavioural change: zero, plus a contract that now lies to the model about how its output is consumed. And if 728 *is* changed (unbudgeted), `[x]` collides with three live meanings: write_review's own published legend (`[x]` resolved / `[-]` outdated, does not block — a non-blocking state **already exists** and the proposal ignores it); `preserve_prior` (review.sh:633-642), which warns on `^- \[(x|-)\] F` to mean "human judgements are being overwritten," a warning that would then fire on every same-SHA re-review; and review.md §12, where "every box ticked" means *disposed and converted to a tracked issue*. Reviewer-ticked advisories are ticked and untracked, so nothing can tell disposition from advisory.

**3. The round-3 suppression rule lets real defects merge — counterexample from the record.** PR 5 round 3 (`99ccb0c1`, 08:21) is **4 findings, all severity `changes`, zero blockers**: redundant transitive imports, an empty second public name `binaryEquiv`, a `polyFunc` abbreviation duplicating the LDT declaration *contrary to the binding brief*, and duplicated question-supports. Under "from round 3 only blocker-severity net-new findings may be added; anything lesser goes in the ## Review prose," all four move to prose and the ledger becomes `<!-- no findings -->`, unresolved=0. Two branches, both worse:
- reviewer keeps CHANGES_REQUESTED → gate 4 blocks with an **empty checklist**; the operator has nothing to tick, §12 adjudication has no "last round's findings" to list, and convergence is impossible — churn goes up, not down;
- reviewer downgrades to COMMENTED (which the trusted task line 101, "advisory items alone do not block approval," positively invites once the ledger is empty) → `unresolved=0` + COMMENTED → review.sh posts `local-review/summary=success` and gate 4 passes. **PR 5 merges with four unfixed defects and zero tracked issues.** Round 3 is the single round in the entire corpus with no blockers, and it is the round immediately before PR 5's only-ever APPROVED (`b5da371d`, 0 findings, 08:57) — the proposal fires exactly where the loop was about to work. Same for PR 7 round 4 (`16116ab4`, 7 blocker + 10 changes): ten changes-level findings demoted to prose on the last round before adjudication, breaking §12's closing invariant, "Nothing is dropped silently: an adjudicated finding lives on as an issue" — only ledger lines become issues.

**4. The round counter is unsound as derived.** Counting marker-bound reviews counts *distinct reviewed head SHAs*, not review rounds. `post_review` (gh_common.py:242-260) is idempotent per commit_id, so same-SHA re-reviews are fine — but `autofix.sh` pushes to the PR branch (lines 590 and 875), and each push creates a new head → ci.sh → a fresh marker-bound review. A PR with two operator rounds and three autofix pushes reads as round 5: it gets the adjudication banner and the blocker-only suppression before a human has responded even twice.

**5. Wrong lens for the cost claim, and it pushes the dominant cost driver the wrong way.** It touches none of the three measured drivers (20 KB `MAX_CONTEXT_BYTES` diff truncation, no wall-clock/turn budget, 83.8% of tool-output bytes outside the diff). Worse: "this is round N of at most 4" and "only *net-new* findings" both require knowing what prior rounds said, and review.sh supplies no previous ledger while the trusted task's own channels for it (`gh pr diff`, `get_review_comments`, GraphQL `reviewThreads`) are forbidden by the local contract at review.sh:634. The measured consequence of that exact gap is PR 21's 50 commands / 5.0 MB / ~19 min mining `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews` for old ledgers. This proposal strengthens the incentive on that pathology without opening the channel.

**6. Latent gate break in the banner.** review.sh:869-871 documents that the gate regex is applied to "the whole combined body, not just the ledger — so a stray `- [ ]` bullet in a reviewer's prose counts for both or neither." §12 verbatim is numbered (1.-4.) and safe, but any bulleted paraphrase of it in a round-5 banner ("- [ ] post an ADJUDICATION comment") silently increments `unresolved` on a line no one can ever tick, making the PR permanently un-greenable.",

### Motivation

Discharge the external Magic Square self-testing boundary used by QPBT
soundness. The canonical project statement is `thm:ms-rigidity` in
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`,
matched by `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:224-253`. The cited
external source is Coladangelo--Stark, arXiv:1709.09267v2, Theorem 6.9.

The cited external proof obtains this as a robust linear-constraint-system
self-test using its general solution-group/stability machinery. This repository
has no such general framework. Formalize only the finite-dimensional Magic
Square consequence needed here; do not introduce a project-wide LCS or
approximate-representation mechanism.

### Target

After the Magic Square foundation/split packet #75, prove only the existing
`MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ms_rigidity` in
`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/MagicSquareTheorems.lean`, preserving its complete public
signature verbatim:

- one universal `C : ℝ` with `1 ≤ C`, before `ε` and `S`;
- every `ε ≥ 0` and every `S : Strategy msGame` with `1 - ε ≤ S.value`;
- an `MsRigidityWitness S`;
- the Euclidean state bound;
- Alice and Bob measurement-distance bounds at zero-based variables 0/X and
  4/Z;
- both anticommutator-distance bounds;
- all seven bounds at scale `C * Real.sqrt ε`.

### Dependencies

- Base on merged #75.
- Base on #49 for the clean state-dependent distance/observable conversion and
  triangle API, especially `opFamilyDistSq_le_of_le_of_le`,
  `consistencyDefect_postprocess_le`, and `povm_to_obs` where applicable.
- Base on #64 for clean EPR normalization and the Pauli-projector/observable
  expansions used to identify `idealMagicBitProj`.
- Base on #68 for the binary Pauli involution and twisted-commutation laws.
- It is independent of the perfect-strategy packet, #69, the fixed-field-model
  work, and encoding/decoding. Once the split and these three dependencies
  land, rigidity and perfect strategy may run concurrently in disjoint files.

### Proof route

1. Expand the game value over the 36 directed constraint-variable incidences.
   Convert `1 - ε ≤ S.value` into rejection-mass bounds, then into the
   finitely many row/column consistency relations with explicit constants.
   Include bounds for wrong-form answers folded by `msBitOrZero`; they are not
   definitionally absent.
2. Reduce arbitrary finite POVMs to projective measurements without
   strengthening the theorem. Reuse or adapt the proved one-measurement and
   tensor-product Naimark machinery in
   `MIPStarRE/LDT/MakingMeasurementsProjective/NaimarkFull.lean`, but prove the
   pure-vector/intertwining consequences actually needed here: value
   preservation, composition of the input-space embeddings with the eventual
   self-test isometries, and transfer of state-dependent effect bounds back to
   the original strategy.
3. For the dilated projective strategy, turn the six nearly satisfied parity
   constraints and same-cell agreement into approximate reflection relations.
   Isolate a proved, file-local projective Magic Square rigidity lemma;
   projectivity must be discharged by step 2, not exposed in
   `exists_ms_rigidity`.
4. Follow the finite Magic Square operator argument: extract approximate Pauli
   `X` and `Z` pairs for the two logical qubits, construct the local swap
   isometries, and obtain a normalized auxiliary vector. Keep all intermediate
   relation/error lemmas concrete and proved. Do not restate
   Coladangelo--Stark's general theorem as an axiom or assumed proposition.
5. Translate the cited theorem's ideal observables `I⊗Z` and `ZX⊗ZX` through
   the explicit local basis change to the project's `X⊗I` and `Z⊗I`. Use
   #64/#68 to identify the corresponding
   binary effects with `idealMagicBitProj`.
6. Convert the self-test's density/trace estimate to the exact Euclidean vector
   estimate. Account for the square-root loss explicitly; this is not a
   definitional `simpa`.
7. Derive the four `msOperatorDistanceA/B` bounds, then the two
   `msAnticommutatorDistanceA/B` bounds from binary observable expansion,
   multiplication stability, and the squared-distance triangle estimates from
   #49.
8. Track explicit constants throughout and take a finite maximum to obtain the
   single universal `C ≥ 1`. Handle the theorem's unrestricted `ε ≥ 0`: use
   the robust argument in its small-error range and a separately
   proved coarse large-error bound with canonical padded isometries. Do not
   silently assume `ε ≤ 1`.

Private implementation submodules under
`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/MagicSquareTheorems/Rigidity/` are allowed when they keep
individual proofs reviewable. They remain owned by this one issue and must
bottom out in Lean/Mathlib and the already proved local APIs.

### Statement integrity

Paper assumptions: an arbitrary finite-dimensional strategy whose Magic Square
success is `1-ε`. Lean uses arbitrary finite local carriers, a unit pure state,
arbitrary POVMs, nonnegative `ε`, and a lower success bound; the

### Motivation

Prove the converse Magic Square construction `thm:ms-from-ac`: any exact
anticommuting pair of consistent binary projective measurements extends to a
value-one SPCC Magic Square strategy. The canonical statement and full
operator-table proof are
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:654-878`;
the matched blueprint node is
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:255-286`.

After the Magic Square foundation/split packet #75, prove only the existing
declaration `MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ms_perfect_strategy_of_anticommuting` in
`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/MagicSquareTheorems/PerfectStrategy.lean`, preserving its
signature verbatim.

In particular preserve arbitrary finite nonempty `ι`, the hypotheses `hA`,
`hB`, `hcA`, `hcB`, and `hac`, and every exact conclusion: `S.ι = ι × ZMod 2`,
`S.IsSPCC`, value `1`, state `msPerfectState ι`, and the
variable-0/variable-4 effect embeddings.

- Base on merged #75.
- Base on #64 for the clean `eprState_norm` theorem used to normalize
  `msPerfectState`.

  encoding/decoding. If #68 is already merged, reuse a directly applicable
  binary identity only when it avoids local duplication; do not make it a hard
  dependency or introduce type-reindexing infrastructure merely to use it.

### Proof route

1. From `hA` and `hB`, establish locally that `obsOf A` and `obsOf B` are
   Hermitian involutions and recover each binary effect as
   `(1 ± obsOf _)/2`.
2. Define the single-qubit `X` and `Z` observables on `ZMod 2` from the existing
   concrete Pauli matrices, or equivalent private entrywise definitions. Prove
   their Hermiticity, involution, exact anticommutation, and consistency on
   `eprState (ZMod 2)` by finite extensional calculation.
3. Define the nine cell observables exactly as the paper's table:

   `OA⊗I, I⊗X, OA⊗X; I⊗Z, OB⊗I, OB⊗Z; OA⊗Z, OB⊗X, OA*OB⊗Z*X`.

4. Use `hac` and `XZ = -ZX` to prove that the bottom-right cell is Hermitian
   and squares to one. Prove pairwise commutation within all six rows/columns,
   and that their products are `I` except for the final column, whose product
   is `-I`.
5. Turn each Hermitian involution into its binary PVM. For variable questions,
   embed `.bit b` and assign zero to `.triple _`.
6. For each constraint, define the joint triple PVM by multiplying the three
   commuting cell projections. Embed `.triple beta` and assign zero to `.bit

9. Prove value one supportwise: parity follows from the six row/column product

   marginal. Sum accepted outcomes to one using measurement completeness and

10. Finish the exact variable-0 and variable-4 effect equalities by unfolding
    the construction; do not replace them with observable-only equalities.

Keep all operator-table, reflection-to-PVM, and finite-index lemmas private or
file-local.

## Code review

**F1-F2.** Both scripts bind evidence to `HEAD_SHA` but execute against the live worktree without requiring it to be clean. An uncommitted repair can make CI pass for code absent from GitHub; dirty contextual files can similarly hide findings from a reviewer. Refuse dirty worktrees before publication, or use an isolated checkout of the exact SHA.

**F3-F4.** CI marks only step contexts pending, while `review.sh` trusts the old `local-ci/summary=success`. Review rerequests are worse: `gh_common.post_review` keeps the old body, while `post_summary` merely warns on publication failure. An old approved body and green status can therefore survive a newly adverse review. Invalidate summaries with a fatal `pending` write before reruns, replace the published ledger, and make final status publication fatal.

**F5-F6.** After waiting for the fix lock, `autofix.sh` rechecks only the remote head. A superseded run can leave a newer local commit unpushed, after which the waiter operates on that commit using the old head’s statuses and count. Separately, reaching the cap between phases invokes terminal review before the accumulated commit reaches GitHub, then exits without pushing it. Recompute local/remote state and the cap under the lock, and route cap completion through push, CI, then exact-head review.

**F7.** The implementation defaults to `auto-fix-codex`, while `local/protocols/autofix.md` and the taxonomy specify `auto-fix-claude`. The cap ritual also never removes that label, so its supposedly once-only review can repeat. Use one documented label and remove it when the cap is reached.

**F8.** `/issues/N` also returns pull requests. Falling back after transport, authentication, or server failures can therefore classify a PR as an issue and select `main` for a write-enabled agent. Fall back only on a proven 404, and reject an issue response containing `pull_request`.

**F9.** The regex misses `Closes: #42` and qualified same-repository references, while the gate scans no commit messages. GitHub documents all of these as closing surfaces, so a parent with open sub-issues can still be closed on merge. Expand both the parser and scanned inputs, with regression tests. See [GitHub’s closing-keyword syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue?apiVersion=2022-11-28).

**F10-F11.** `--adjudicated` checks only a prefix and current-head token; it does not establish four completed rounds or require checked, dispositioned findings and issue references. Gate 1 also accepts absent/null `draft`, contrary to `local/protocols/issues-prs.md:84-85`. Validate the complete adjudication record and require `draft is False`.

**F12.** `post_merge` refreshes `origin/main` and starts the warmer even if `fast_forward_base` refused divergent history. That can make future diff audits use the wrong base. Continue alias refresh, warming, and cleanup only after verified fast-forward, or bind the alias directly to the verified fetched GitHub base.

**F13-F14.** A change limited to `gh_common.py`, `wf_util.py`, `review.sh`, or `pr_merge.py` can produce eight skipped-success contexts without running `test_github_workflow.py`. Additionally, issue keys are optional, keyed adoption searches only 100 issues, and branch queries are not URL-encoded. Broaden workflow gating, require stable issue keys, paginate adoption, and encode query parameters.

**F15-F17.** The issue quick-start omits its required body argument, while the PR quick-start permits a footer-only body despite the mandatory three-section template. Scout instructions still alternately require editing/committing an issue file and returning a GitHub comment; moved briefs retain dead `issues/briefs/...` links. Finally, the hook’s per-commit count and “split the change” advice contradict the normative 400-line per-episode cap. Align these operator-facing contracts before merge.

No Lean or blueprint declarations changed, so source-statement fidelity and `sorry` review are not applicable. `git diff --check`, shell syntax checks, and Python AST parsing passed. The unit suite could not be rerun in this read-only sandbox because its temporary-directory setup had no writable location; the attached exact-head CI status reports success.

   377	   language rule for Lean documentation and public names. Reviewers should flag

## Findings

- [ ] F1 (blocker) `local/bin/review.sh:600` — Fresh-base carry-forward can republish the oldest duplicate ledger and certify stale review evidence

## Review

The repeated prior F1 is resolved for direct publication: `post_review` now updates `matching[-1]`, consistent with the chronological ordering guaranteed by GitHub’s [reviews endpoint](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews), `pr_merge.py`, and `autofix.sh`.

The duplicate case is still unsafe end to end. `review.sh:577-588` identifies the newest valid source review, but retains only its head SHA. Lines 600-609 then rescan the original chronological list and stop at the first body containing that head, which is the oldest duplicate. Given an older clean review followed by a newer adverse review, carry-forward republishes the clean ledger and posts `local-review/summary=success` at lines 632-637. The resulting exact-head evidence can pass the merge gate despite the operative source review being adverse.

Carry-forward should retain the exact selected review row, or repeat the newest-first selection with the same marker, commit, author, and non-carried checks. Add regression coverage for an older clean duplicate followed by a newer adverse duplicate; the added test currently exercises only `post_review`.

`git diff --check`, shell syntax validation, and Python AST parsing passed. The focused unit test could not run in this read-only sandbox because no writable temporary directory was available; the trusted task context reports exact-head CI green. No Lean or blueprint files changed.

VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUESTED
